exclusions.MIXDOG_PROVIDER_WS_HEDGE_MS / MIXDOG_PRO: module-load constants of the Node tree; every scenario runs on the defaults (3000 ms hedge, 15000 ms acquire). The core reads the same settings through the adapter context and its tests use the defaults too
exclusions.dial events of a connection that never a: the Codex route warms its connection with a plain HTTP request on the first acquire (preconnect), which dials once without being a WebSocket leg; the core runs that warm-up on its HTTP client, apart from the dial, so only the legs are compared
exclusions.events of kind closed: the server's view of a closed connection. In Node a cancelled stuck leg (`socket.terminate()` before the upgrade) leaves its loopback connection open, the core drops the dial and closes it; the other closes follow the recorder's own release of the opened socket. Not compared: the replay compares the upgrades the server saw, when, and how the acquire ended
exclusions.events of kind opened: the server completing the upgrade; the same fact as the upgrade whose action is open
exclusions.events of kind upgrade: the server's view of a request arriving, in real I/O time after the dial; the dial events (the product asking for a connection, at the virtual time of the leg's start) are compared instead
exclusions.outcome.message of a transport failure (: the text is `ws`/libuv wording for the reset the recorder wrote; the core states the typed transport fault and its own words. The replay compares that the race ended, when, and with a transport (not status, not acquire-timeout) failure

product.tree: product tree loaded by the recorder
